omar (Customer): Hey support — after rotating our Redwood API key via Vault last night, our prod app started getting 401s from the API around 04:12 UTC. Errors look like `401: invalid_api_key`. Not all requests fail; about 40% succeed and 60% get 401. We rotated by writing to `secret/redwood/apikey` and marking old version revoked. Any idea?

lina (Support): sorry you're hitting this, omar. quick Qs: did you rotate using KV v2 or v1? did you hit the API key rotation endpoint from the Redwood console or directly update Vault? can you paste the exact Vault path/JSON you wrote (redact the key) and a sample error trace?

omar (Customer): we used our Vault UI — path `secret/data/redwood/apikey` (KV v2). we wrote a JSON with `data: { api_key: "redacted" }` using the UI. error trace: `2026-03-14T04:12:18Z GET /v1/chat/gen -> 401 invalid_api_key (x-request-id: ... )`

ken (Oncall): odd that some requests still succeed. sounds like some processes have the new key and some still use old. Could be propagation to sidecars or env var sync. omar, how many app replicas? deployment uses sidecar that reads Vault and injects env var?

omar (Customer): 6 pods behind an internal LB. we use a sidecar that mounts secrets from Vault into env vars at startup, not a hot refresh. we *expected* the rotation to cause sidecar to trigger a refresh webhook from our infra. we called `vault kv put secret/redwood/apikey api_key="newkey"` (via CLI) and set `revoke_previous=true` in our rotation script.

lina (Support): can you run `curl -s -H "X-Vault-Token: $TOKEN" https://vault.example/v1/secret/data/redwood/apikey | jq .` and paste the top-level keys? common gotcha: KV v2 returns `data` with nested `data` object, i.e., `.data.data.api_key`. Our propagation agent expects the API key at `.data.api_key` (KV v1). If your vault is v2, the agent could be reading the wrong path and not updating pods, leaving some pods with stale keys.

omar (Customer): running now... output: `{ "request_id": "...", "data": { "data": { "api_key": "new-opaque-key", "meta": {} }, "metadata": { "version": 2 } } }` — ohhh.

vault-proxy (bot): secret change event: secret/data/redwood/apikey @ 2026-03-14T04:11:59Z - version 2 (KV v2)

ken (Oncall): bingo. so our webhook processor is likely hitting `.data.api_key` and getting null, so old key remained in injected pods. Some pods were redeployed so they picked up new key (hence partial success).

omar (Customer): confirmed. two pods restarted during the window, they show successful requests. other pods still 401.

lina (Support): immediate remediation: 1) set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var on the deployment to the new key and do a rolling restart. 2) or run `kubectl delete pod` for the remaining pods to force them to pick up the injected env on start. Temporary fix until we patch.

omar (Customer): will do rolling restart now.

(10m later)

omar (Customer): rolling restart done. 0 401s now. thanks.

lina (Support): great. long-term fix: our rotation webhook parsing needs to support KV v2. I'm opening an internal ticket to update the agent and add a detection fallback to read both `.data.api_key` and `.data.data.api_key`. Also we'll add a health check in the agent that warns when the secret path returns unexpected JSON.

jay (eng-runtime): tagging eng-runtime — we should also add an automatic "missing key" alert that surface if the agent returns null for the configured key path. I'll take the code change.

lina (Support): follow-ups for runbook: - doc note for customers to mention their Vault KV version when they file rotation requests - add CLI helper `rw-secret-verify` that checks both path variants and returns the actual value existence - add unit test for KV v1/v2 shapes.

omar (Customer): appreciated. and FYI we set TTL for old key revoke at 0, so immediate revocation expected. we can keep rotate+restart as part of process until patch lands.

lina (Support): noted. closing the incident once eng runtime confirms PR. thanks all :tada:
